transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-04
- Time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~45m
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Li (Redwood Solutions), Daniel (CTO, Stonebridge), Priya (Eng Manager), Carlos (Network Lead)

Summary:
Quick discovery for Private/VPC deployment options. Customer evaluating Private (VPC) vs Dedicated; main concerns: network/topology, region constraints, CIDR overlap, private endpoints vs peering, KMS integration, audit logs, timeline and cost.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: ok thanks everyone for joining, im maya from redwood inference, i handle the account, i'm joined by ethan our se and li from solutions. hows everyone doing?
[00:10] Daniel: good thanks, uh excited to dig in. we want to understand networking options and security posture before we commit to a pilot.
[00:18] Maya: great, quick reminder, this call is discovery - we'll capture constraints, stakeholders and next steps. to kick off daniel could you run through current infra and what you're trying to achieve?
[00:30] Daniel: sure. stonebridge is a mid sized fintech, most infra in aws us-east-1. we have a prod vpc, monitoring vpc, and a separate data lake in a different account. primary use case is private LLM inference for sensitive customer documents - must not egress to public internet. latency target is sub 150ms p95 for key routes, and we're evaluating whether redwood private in our VPC or a dedicated redwood offering makes more sense.
[00:55] Priya: and from engineering side we want a setup that supports canary rollouts and model pinning, plus ease of ops - ideally CI/CD friendly and low touch. also we need KMS integration and audit logs retained for 1 year minimum.
[01:12] Ethan: yeah good context. a few quick clarifying q's - is your VPC in a single account/region or multiple? any constraints on IP ranges?
[01:20] Carlos: single account for prod in us-east-1 but we will expand to eu-west-1 for residency later this year. we currently use 10.1.0.0/16 in prod, 10.2.0.0/16 in data. we want to avoid overlapping CIDR with any vendor peering.
[01:36] Maya: ok noted. two main network topologies we typically recommend: VPC peering (transitive limitations) or private endpoints via AWS PrivateLink/VPCE with interface endpoints. both have tradeoffs on cross-account routing, egress, and NAT.
[01:55] Daniel: can you explain differences quickly? we heard conflicting advice internally about peering vs private link.
[02:02] Ethan: sure. with VPC peering you establish a direct peering connection between your VPC and Redwood's VPC; it's simple, low-latency, but peering is not transitive and can be tricky if you have many accounts or need cross-region - you'd pair per region. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) exposes a private ENI in your VPC that connects to our service endpoints, avoids router-level peering and is easier for cross-account and supports security group control. however it can add per-GB data processing charges and slightly higher latency compared to intra-VPC peering.
[02:34] Priya: what about egress and internet access? we want no egress to internet for inference traffic.
[02:40] Ethan: both approaches can be configured to avoid public internet egress; with PrivateLink traffic stays inside aws backbone, with peering you can control via routing tables and nat gateways - the key is ensuring we don't provide a public endpoint and that flows are restricted by SGs and route tables.
[02:57] Carlos: and IP overlap - if our CIDR overlaps with Redwood's, can we use NAT or a proxy?
[03:05] Ethan: overlapping CIDRs are painful. we usually recommend either choosing a non overlapping range or using AWS Transit Gateway with NAT or SNATing at a proxy. Transit Gateway adds complexity and cost. we can also host Redwood in your VPC (customer-hosted deployment) to avoid peering but that is a larger project.
[03:25] Maya: note that for on-prem or air-gapped installs we have an on-prem package but it requires our ops work and longer timeline. for typical private vpc installs timeline is 2-4 weeks for onboarding network connectivity and configuration, depending on approvals.
[03:40] Daniel: ok timeline is important - we have a compliance window in Q2. we also need key management - can we integrate with our KMS / HSM?
[03:48] Ethan: yes we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and we can integrate via cross-account grants; for HSM a couple customers have used bring-your-own HSM with extra integration work. we'll need security team sign-off and a walkthrough.
[04:03] Priya: audit logs - how are they exposed? we need syslogs/audit events sent to our S3 and CloudWatch with one year retention.
[04:11] Li: we stream audit logs to customer S3 buckets or to our logging endpoints; retention policies are configurable and you can set lifecycle rules. we also offer audit trail exports and can push to SIEM via Kinesis if needed.
[04:26] Carlos: network ports - what ports and IP ranges do you require? also do you need inbound rules?
[04:33] Ethan: we typically require outbound HTTPS (443) to our service endpoints when using PrivateLink; for peering we ask to allow specific ports between the peered subnets (we'll provide exact ranges). you'll also need to allow TCP traffic for the control plane on a few management ports; we'll provide a minimal checklist.
[04:50] Daniel: region constraints - you said Redwood can run in multiple regions. can the same account have Redwood private in us-east-1 and eu-west-1?
[04:58] Maya: yes you can deploy private instances per region; we recommend separate VPC peering/private endpoints per region. If you need cross-region failover, we can discuss replication and routing policies; that typically increases cost.
[05:12] Priya: tradeoffs - latency vs cost. we saw mention of quantized models to reduce compute: how does that affect private deployment?
[05:20] Ethan: quantization is orthogonal to networking - it reduces GPU footprint so lowers cost. in private deployments you can pick model variants and quant profiles; runtime will pick kernels accordingly. for strict latency SLOs we may recommend dedicated capacity or co-located hosts in your VPC.
[05:36] Daniel: are there any compliance docs you can share now? SOC2, ISO, penetration test reports?
[05:42] Maya: yes we'll share SOC2, pen test summary, network checklist and our private deployment runbook. I'll attach links in an email.
[05:50] Carlos: what about SSO and RBAC? we use Okta and need SAML + SCIM provisioning.
[05:56] Li: we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC is integrated into the console and audit logs map to user actions. we can also integrate with your IDP for service accounts.
[06:08] Daniel: pricing - do you have pilot pricing for private deployments? we dont want a big commitment yet.
[06:14] Maya: yes typically we do a time-limited pilot (30-90 days) with usage caps, or a short reserved node commit if you want steady capacity. I'll send a pilot proposal and pricing tiers.
[06:26] Priya: network peering vs private link latency numbers? any benchmarks?
[06:30] Ethan: we've observed peering intra-region p95 in the 20-40ms range to our infra depending on network, private link closer to 30-60ms - these are rough; we'll run a quick benchmark during the technical deep dive.
[06:46] Daniel: great if you can run a perf check from our VPC to your target region that would be helpful.
[06:52] Maya: yes we'll propose a bench plan - small corpus, 1k requests, measure p50/p95 and token costs.
[07:00] Carlos: do you support GCP or azure private endpoints if we expand?
[07:05] Ethan: we currently support AWS PrivateLink and peering; for GCP it's VPC peering or private service connect and for Azure private endpoints we have a roadmap and some early pilots. we should confirm for your future multi-cloud plan.
[07:20] Priya: ok who will be involved from your side for a tech deep dive? we want network plus se.
[07:25] Maya: ethan will lead the network/arch review, li will cover security and audit, and myself for pilot/pricing.
[07:33] Daniel: any known gotchas? we've had trouble before with provider side NAT, source IP preservation, and outage blast radius.
[07:41] Ethan: good point - with peering you preserve source IP which helps logging, with PrivateLink you might see SNAT depending on setup. we'll document behaviors. also on outage blast radius we have routing fallbacks and multi-region options to reduce impact but that costs more.
[07:58] Maya: ok let's recap next steps: we'll send network checklist + security pack, schedule deep dive next week, propose pilot scope and pricing, and run a perf test from daniel's VPC. any other items?
[08:10] Daniel: can you include a short diagram of recommended topology for our case (single prod VPC to Redwood in us-east-1 with eu-west future)?
[08:18] Ethan: yes i'll include diagrams showing peering vs PrivateLink and transit gateway option.
[08:22] Carlos: i'll confirm CIDR availability and any peering restrictions and follow up.
[08:28] Maya: perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up by email with docs and proposed times for the deep dive.
[08:33] Daniel: thanks all.

End of transcript.
